rule.title: Container With A hostPath Mount Created
rule.author: Leo Tsaousis (@laripping)

es.summary: Se creó un pod en Kubernetes que monta un directorio o archivo del nodo mediante un volumen hostPath. Puede ser legítimo (DaemonSets de sistema) o un intento de escapar del contenedor hacia el nodo.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos del audit log de Kubernetes con verb 'create' sobre objectRef.resource 'pods' en los que el campo hostPath tiene un valor, es decir, el pod declara un volumen hostPath.
es.why_it_matters: Un hostPath con permisos de escritura, sobre todo de '/' o de rutas sensibles como /etc, /var/run/docker.sock o /var/lib/kubelet, permite hacer chroot al nodo, leer secretos o controlar el runtime. Esto corresponde a escape a host (ATT&CK T1611) y escalamiento de privilegios.
triage_steps: Identifique al solicitante en user.username, sus grupos y sourceIPs. Distinga cuentas de servicio de controladores (system:serviceaccount:kube-system:daemon-set-controller) de usuarios humanos o tokens externos.
Revise objectRef.namespace y objectRef.name. Las creaciones fuera de kube-system o de namespaces de agentes conocidos (monitoreo, CNI, CSI) merecen más atención.
Examine la ruta de hostPath y el requestObject: verifique si monta '/', /etc, /root, /var/run/docker.sock, containerd.sock o /var/lib/kubelet, y si readOnly es falso.
Revise el resto del spec: privileged, hostPID, hostNetwork, hostIPC, runAsUser 0, la imagen usada y comandos como chroot, nsenter o shells inversos.
Verifique si el pod pertenece a un DaemonSet, Deployment o Job conocido (ownerReferences) y si coincide con un cambio aprobado o un pipeline de GitOps.
Pivote por el mismo usuario y sourceIPs en ±15 minutos: busque exec/attach sobre el pod, lectura de secrets, creación de rolebindings o pruebas de permisos (selfsubjectaccessreviews).
Consulte alertas anteriores del mismo usuario, namespace o nodo, y revise los logs del nodo donde se programó el pod.
false_positives: El controlador de DaemonSet crea pods con hostPath en kube-system (kube-proxy, CNI, recolectores de logs).
Agentes de monitoreo, seguridad o almacenamiento (exportadores de nodo, drivers CSI, EDR para contenedores) desplegados en sus propios namespaces.
Administradores que depuran nodos con pods temporales aprobados, por ejemplo mediante kubectl debug node.
response_steps: Confirme con el dueño del workload o del namespace si el pod y su montaje hostPath estaban autorizados.
Si no está autorizado, preserve el manifiesto y los logs, y luego elimine el pod; aísle o acordone (cordon) el nodo afectado mientras investiga.
Revoque o rote las credenciales del usuario o la cuenta de servicio usada y revise sus RoleBindings y ClusterRoleBindings.
Revise el nodo en busca de persistencia (cron, claves SSH, binarios modificados) y rote los secretos expuestos en el nodo.
Aplique Pod Security Admission (baseline/restricted) o políticas de admisión que restrinjan hostPath a namespaces y rutas aprobadas.
es.severity_rationale: El nivel bajo es adecuado porque los pods con hostPath son comunes en cargas de sistema; el riesgo aumenta con rutas sensibles, escritura, privilegios o un solicitante inusual.

en.summary: A Kubernetes pod was created that mounts a node directory or file through a hostPath volume. This may be a legitimate system DaemonSet or an attempt to escape from the container to the node.
en.what_it_detects: Kubernetes audit events with verb 'create' on objectRef.resource 'pods' where the hostPath field has a value, meaning the pod declares a hostPath volume.
en.why_it_matters: A writable hostPath, especially of '/' or sensitive paths such as /etc, /var/run/docker.sock or /var/lib/kubelet, lets an attacker chroot into the node, read secrets or control the runtime. This is escape to host (ATT&CK T1611) and privilege escalation.
triage_steps: Identify the requester from user.username, groups and sourceIPs. Separate controller service accounts (system:serviceaccount:kube-system:daemon-set-controller) from human users or external tokens.
Check objectRef.namespace and objectRef.name. Creations outside kube-system or known agent namespaces (monitoring, CNI, CSI) need closer review.
Inspect the hostPath path and requestObject: does it mount '/', /etc, /root, /var/run/docker.sock, containerd.sock or /var/lib/kubelet, and is readOnly false?
Review the rest of the spec: privileged, hostPID, hostNetwork, hostIPC, runAsUser 0, the image, and commands such as chroot, nsenter or reverse shells.
Check whether the pod belongs to a known DaemonSet, Deployment or Job (ownerReferences) and matches an approved change or GitOps pipeline.
Pivot on the same user and sourceIPs within +/- 15 minutes: exec/attach on the pod, secret reads, new rolebindings or permission probing (selfsubjectaccessreviews).
Look for earlier alerts on the same user, namespace or node, and review logs on the node where the pod was scheduled.
false_positives: The DaemonSet controller creates pods with hostPath volumes in kube-system (kube-proxy, CNI, log collectors).
Monitoring, security or storage agents (node exporters, CSI drivers, container EDR) deployed in their own namespaces.
Administrators debugging nodes with approved temporary pods, for example via kubectl debug node.
response_steps: Confirm with the workload or namespace owner whether the pod and its hostPath mount were authorized.
If unauthorized, preserve the manifest and logs, then delete the pod; cordon or isolate the affected node while investigating.
Revoke or rotate credentials of the user or service account involved and review its RoleBindings and ClusterRoleBindings.
Check the node for persistence (cron, SSH keys, modified binaries) and rotate secrets exposed on that node.
Enforce Pod Security Admission (baseline/restricted) or admission policies that restrict hostPath to approved namespaces and paths.
en.severity_rationale: Low fits because hostPath pods are common for system workloads; risk rises with sensitive paths, write access, privileges or an unusual requester.

positive.description: A user creates a pod in the default namespace that mounts the node root filesystem through hostPath.
Service account creates a pod mounting the container runtime socket via hostPath.

negative.description: Pod creation that only uses emptyDir and configMap volumes, with no hostPath field.
Reading an existing pod that has a hostPath volume (verb get, not create).
